title: Statements of Benefit Charges and Written Protests under Employer Benefit Charging
content:
**Section 1 — Statements.** Under Employer Benefit Charging, a statement of benefit charges is mailed for each quarter in which charges or credits were posted, no later than the statement mailing days after the quarter ends (45 calendar days in every charge class), by mail and in the employer portal, listing each claimant's charges by week.

**Section 2 — Right to protest.** The employer may protest the charges on a statement in writing through the employer portal, by fax or by mail.

**Section 3 — Protest window.** A protest is accepted only when it is received no later than the protest window after the statement mailing date. The window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the statement mailing date, and a protest received on the last day is timely. The protest window is 30 calendar days in every charge class.

(a) The clock starts from the mailing date of that quarter's statement as recorded for the employer's position; the record of the statement for that position and quarter is the evidence, not the employer's recollection of when it arrived.
(b) Day one is the day after the statement mailing date; the last day is the thirtieth calendar day after it.
(c) A protest received on or before the last day is accepted; a protest received after it is not.

| Hypothetical statement mailing date | Protest received | Accepted |
|---|---|---|
| 14 May | 13 June (the last day) | Yes |
| 14 May | 14 June | No |
| 1 August | 31 August (the last day) | Yes |
| 1 August | 1 September | No |

**Section 4 — No reargument.** A protest may raise only a ground not already decided: a separation the agency or an appeal has already ruled on cannot be reargued by protest and is challenged only by appeal on the employer benefit charge docket.

**Section 5 — Decision.** A protest is decided within the protest decision business days (30 business days in every charge class); a granted protest relieves the position, and a denied protest leaves it chargeable and may be appealed.

| Protest outcome | Position afterwards | Further remedy |
|---|---|---|
| Granted | Relieved | — |
| Denied | Chargeable | Appeal |

**Basis note.** A protest received within the window may still raise only a ground not already decided under Section 4; a separation already ruled on is challenged only by appeal on the employer benefit charge docket.
